summary: Not published and not flippable in its present form as a benchmark with an enforced isolated-rows protocol. The independent pre-flip audit (2026-10-28, DO NOT PUBLISH) confirmed the construction and every published figure reproduce, but demonstrated that the shipped runner contract passes the whole eval feature table to the predictor (validate.py line 23, byte-identical to the benchmark task template), so the declared isolated_rows mitigation is not enforced at runtime: a frozen label-blind cross-row join (corridor year T -> T+1, copy surged_recently) recovers eval AUC 0.975325 from eval features alone, holdout AUC 0.983034 from holdout features alone, and 0.996970 using all splits with exactly one error; a second frozen attack recovers the target-year count from next-year apps_d / two-years-later apps_d1 exactly (1,625 eval, 1,259 holdout labels, zero errors; full-split AUCs 0.999541 and 0.977654). Descriptor corrections are also required: the missing-history exclusion count is 377 (314/31/32), not 386; target_date values are December-31 calendar identifiers of the outcome year, not publication timestamps; the runner consumes 14 inputs including target_date and surge_cluster while quality.json declares 12 features. Reopen conditions: demonstrable runtime isolation in the shipped contract plus the corrected timing/count/feature statements, re-qualified and re-audited before any flip.
supported_uses: Retrospective train/validation model-development experiments under the documented timing, vintage and selection limitations

Final evaluation only under a protocol that isolates the labeled holdout from agent development and prevents any later row (in particular the same corridor's next label year) from informing an earlier prediction
unsupported_uses: Use as a benchmark under the claimed enforced isolated-rows protocol: the shipped contract passes the full eval table to the predictor, so the mitigation is unenforced
Claims of verified real-time, operational or point-in-time forecasting validity
Treating development/validation (eval-split) scores as untouched final-test results
Consuming rows without isolation (the panel self-answers across adjacent label years of the same corridor)
Presenting the current-vintage panel values as the values an analyst at each past publication instant would have seen
Quoting the full-model eval AUC without the persistence references and their paired intervals beside it

cross_row_audit.scope: Gate 1.5.0 next_label_year_exposes_outcome on the full artifact (2,439 train / 1,265 eval / 1,239 holdout covered, 0 mismatches), superseded in severity by the independent pre-flip audit 2026-10-28: frozen label-blind donor join reached eval AUC 0.975325 (eval donors, predeclared missing-successor rule) and holdout AUC 0.983034 (holdout donors), 0.996970 all-splits with one error (AFG-TJK-2021); count recovery from next-year apps_d / two-years-later apps_d1 exact on 1,625 eval and 1,259 holdout labels. The exposure is inherent to the panel construction AND unmitigated at runtime by the shipped contract, which passes the whole eval table to the predictor after removing only the target column.

limitations: The HDX resource retains no historical vintages (update history observed 2025-11-05, 2026-02-25, 2026-06-11, 2026-06-19, 2026-06-22, 2026-08-20), so a reverse-history probe is not performable: this is retrospective research over the pinned 2026-08-20 distribution, never a certified historical forecasting setup.

Training-label timing is unverified: the 232-day publication lag is an observed release fact (the 2026-08-20 refresh carries complete data through year 2025), not a row-by-row availability ledger, and publications can slip.

Label-observability censoring excludes corridors whose host files no G/P report at all in the label year (33 rows counted, never labelled) and live-edge label-year-2026 corridors (496 counted); the observed panel is a censored sample of the eligible frame, reported not hidden.

Prevalence is not stationary across the panel (eval label years swing 1.4% to 18.8% positives; train 8.42% -> holdout 11.57%): pooled eval AUC blends regimes, and per-label-year figures are the honest grain.

The runner-contract stock baseline trails both persistence references on the identical eval rows (0.5393 vs 0.5742 momentum and 0.5856 surge flag; paired intervals contain zero, observed gaps negative): no headroom over persistence is demonstrated under this protocol, and the comparison is recorded beside every model figure.
